llm.summary: MemClaw is a coherent memory-management skill, but it asks to broadly replace built-in memory and persist or migrate conversation data without enough explicit user-control safeguards.

dimensions.detail: The skill stores local user, agent, session, preference, entity, personal_info, and instruction memories, and can retrieve full L2 content; that is purpose-aligned but sensitive and broadly scoped.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is disclosed as requiring the memclaw plugin and OpenClaw configuration changes, including disabling built-in memory search; no hidden install or executable payload is present in the skill artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill says to use MemClaw for all memory operations and replace built-in memory, which is broad for a persistent memory system and not limited to explicit user requests or confirmed storage.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Memory writes, session commits, background layer generation, maintenance, pruning, reindexing, and native-memory migration are persistent state-changing actions without clear confirmation, rollback, or sensitive-data minimization guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented tools match the stated purpose: search, browse, store, commit, maintain, and migrate OpenClaw memory.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable making MemClaw the main memory layer for OpenClaw. Review what it may store before use, avoid saving secrets or regulated personal data, set narrow session IDs, and require explicit confirmation before migration, maintenance, pruning, reindexing, or committing sensitive sessions.
llm.findings:
[P3] unexpected: Downgraded: the cited text says the plugin does not send data to external servers, with only configured LLM/embedding providers mentioned for API-key use; the artifact does not instruct exfiltration.
[E1] unexpected: Downgraded: the evidence is a negative privacy claim, not an instruction to transmit data to an external URL.
[SQP-1] expected: Accepted as a Review concern: broad 'use for all memory operations' and replacement of built-in memory are coherent with the product pitch but overbroad for persistent memory without explicit scoping safeguards.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted in context: add_memory, commit_session, maintenance, and migrate are expected memory-plugin operations, but the docs understate persistence, migration, pruning/reindexing side effects, and confirmation expectations.
